headline: The first big trail effort has landed — a long, low-HR day on foot at controlled intensity. This is durability work, not a race pace. The gap between narrative and data has closed.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The signature of this week is a single very long, very controlled effort on foot — hours held almost entirely in the lowest zone, well below your threshold ceiling, which is exactly the shape a durability day should take. Everything around it is small: short easy runs bracketing the long one, and strength holding at its usual light-to-moderate functional rhythm. Step counts remain enormous and, tellingly, are as high on nominal rest days as on training days, so background load never really drops for you. The cardio-load status still reads detraining, but that's a lagging rolling average that hasn't yet absorbed the long day — expect it to swing the other way once this effort is counted. Recovery is the one genuinely mixed signal: the nights around the long effort were short and choppy, consistent with a logistics-heavy window rather than settled trail rhythm.
sections.trends: The medium-term picture is unambiguously building — recent four-week volume is up meaningfully on the prior block, and year-to-date distance is roughly four times where you were at this point last year. That's not a consolidation phase quietly regressing; it's a genuine upward step in running load layered on a consistent strength base. The shape makes sense for someone maintaining year-round hybrid readiness rather than chasing a single peak: base and time-on-feet accumulating, with the long effort this week acting as the durability spike on top of it.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchoring heart rate are unchanged from the baseline, so there's no recent evidence of movement in either direction on the aerobic-ceiling front. That's fine — nothing this block has been doing is built to shift threshold, and a long controlled day won't either. Your speed markers remain a demonstrated capacity sitting in reserve, not something this week was trying to sharpen.
sections.zones: The per-session shapes back up the block's intent cleanly. The long effort sat almost wholly in Z1 with only a sliver higher — textbook durability pacing, no drift into grey-zone territory across many hours, which is the discipline that makes back-to-back days survivable. The short surrounding runs are similarly easy. The one genuine intensity touch in the recent set was a brief hard run earlier this month with real Z4 time — a deliberate sharp effort, distinct in character from everything since. Overall the distribution is appropriate: overwhelmingly aerobic, with intensity used sparingly and intentionally.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions continue to sit low, mostly bottom-zone with occasional brief climbs — consistent with functional work rather than heavy strain, and in line with your own strength-session history. On the running side, the two flavours agree well where they overlap; the one thing worth registering is that the brief high-intensity run showed a much broader zone spread and higher peak than the steady sessions, so the effort character there was clearly different even before you read the pace.
sections.calendar: The clustering of short runs in early August followed by the long single effort reads as a deliberate arrangement — light, frequent touches building into one big day, rather than scattered training. Frequency has stayed dependable across the running and strength streaks both, and the consistency is the quiet asset underneath the volume step-up. The rhythm looks intact, not fragmented.
sections.personal_bests: Nothing this week points toward a PB run — the work has been durability and easy volume, which is orthogonal to your short-distance speed marks. Your 50K best is really an ultra-distance mark, and it's that territory the current block is feeding; if anything gets tested soon it's long-distance durability, not the 5K–half range, which would need a dedicated sharpening block to threaten.

watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status reverses out of its detraining reading once the long effort registers — the speed of that flip is a fair proxy for how hard this day loaded you.
Watch how the day or two after the long effort look: whether easy-run HR sits normal or runs elevated, which will tell you how much the effort actually cost.
Watch whether nightly recovery consolidates now that the logistics-heavy window is passing, since the recent nights are still short and broken.
Watch for any back-to-back long efforts appearing — that's the durability quality this block is genuinely training, and worth confirming in the data.
